labelOrigin: Agent-drafted from reading the code at the pinned commit (CLA-289); pending Brenton's spot-check before counting as ground truth.

questions.question: When I change a value in a store, how do the components that use it find out and re-render?
questions.answerNote: createStoreImpl keeps state plus a Set of listeners; setState merges (Object.assign unless replace) only when !Object.is(next, state) and calls every listener with (state, prev). The React hook useStore wires api.subscribe/getState into React.useSyncExternalStore with the selector, so a component re-renders when its selected slice changes.

questions.question: If I change the shape of the state I save in the browser between releases, what happens to data users already have stored?
questions.answerNote: persist stores {state, version}; on hydrate, if the stored version differs from options.version it calls options.migrate(persistedState, version); with no migrate function it logs that the state couldn't be migrated and doesn't use it. Result is merged (shallow by default, or options.merge) and written back.

questions.question: My component picks several fields out of the store as an object and now re-renders all the time — how do I stop that?
questions.answerNote: Wrap the selector in useShallow: it keeps the previous result in a ref and returns it when shallow(prev, next) says the top-level keys/entries are equal, so useSyncExternalStore sees a stable reference.

questions.question: How should I organise a big store into smaller pieces per feature?
questions.answerNote: Slices pattern guide: write per-feature creator functions (createBearSlice, createFishSlice) that receive (set, get, api) and spread them into one bound store via create((...a) => ({...sliceA(...a), ...sliceB(...a)})); middleware only on the combined store.

questions.question: How can I watch state changes and time-travel through them in the browser's debugging extension?
questions.answerNote: Wrap the creator in the devtools middleware; it connects to window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__, sends each setState with an action name and handles jump/time-travel messages. Needs @redux-devtools/extension types.

questions.question: How is the package built into the different module formats it publishes?
questions.answerNote: package.json build:* scripts run rollup -c --config-<entry> per entry point (vanilla, react, middleware, shallow, traditional…); rollup.config.mjs emits a CommonJS dist/<entry>.js and an ESM dist/esm/<entry>.mjs for each (plus .d.ts for index), aliasing internal imports to zustand/* subpaths.

questions.question: How do I put a store back to how it started, say when a user logs out?
questions.answerNote: Guide pattern: add a reset action that calls set(store.getInitialState()); for many stores keep a set of reset functions. getInitialState is part of StoreApi in vanilla.ts and returns the state captured when the creator first ran.

questions.question: Is there a way to use my own comparison function to decide whether a selected value changed?
questions.answerNote: zustand/traditional exports useStoreWithEqualityFn and createWithEqualityFn, built on useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector from the use-sync-external-store package, taking an equalityFn third argument.

c4Note.note: A single container for a small library is defensible, but it mixes the published library (src/) with two separate example apps (examples/demo, examples/starter, each with their own package.json/Vite config), test setup and root tool configs as if they were peer components. A maintainer would describe the library by its entry points: vanilla core, React bindings, middleware, shallow helpers, and the 'traditional' equality-fn API. The ~50-file docs/ site, which answers most usage questions, is invisible.
expectedContainers: zustand library (src/, published npm package with subpath entry points)
problems: examples/demo (8 components) and examples/starter folded into the library container instead of their own containers
eslint.config.mjs, rollup.config.mjs, vitest.config.mts, examples/starter/vite.config.ts and tests/setup.ts shown as architecture components
src/middleware/*.ts (7 files) and src/middleware.ts not grouped into one 'middleware' component; vanilla/react shallow helpers likewise split
docs/ Markdown (guides + API reference) not represented at all

overviews.note: Tiny library: summary says what it is and to read src/vanilla.ts; key points add middleware typing and rollup gotcha; children is one drill-in link.
Summary and key points carry the whole mental model; the 30 children mix examples and lint config with src so they come after; parent is redundant.
